dimensions.evidence: The Director shall identify real property that is owned or leased by the Federal Government and that contains court accommodations in not more than 10 judicial districts

dimensions.assessment: Shifts major facility management, leasing, and operational authority from the General Services Administration to the judicial branch for specified properties.
dimensions.evidence: transfer to the Director the jurisdiction, custody, and control of any requested real property owned or leased by the United States

dimensions.assessment: Establishes the Judicial Space and Facilities Management Fund in the Treasury using appropriated funds, reimbursements, and deposits, with specific congressional approval thresholds for projects exceeding $5,000,000 or $10,000,000.
dimensions.evidence: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund to be known as the `Judicial Space and Facilities Management Fund'.

dimensions.assessment: Amends titles 28 and 40 of the United States Code to establish a new Judiciary Buildings Service, a dedicated funding mechanism, and specific property transfer and leasing authorities.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a pilot program with a transfer authority sunset after 7 years, an asset return beginning at 10 years, and a full repeal of the act after 15 years.
dimensions.evidence: Effective on the date that is 15 years after the date of enactment of this Act, this Act is repealed

summary: The Judicial Space and Facilities Management Effectiveness Act of 2026 establishes a pilot program allowing the Director of the Administrative Office of the United States Courts to take over jurisdiction, custody, and control of real property and leases containing court accommodations in up to ten judicial districts. It also transfers the Thurgood Marshall Federal Judiciary Building to the Director's control, creates the Judiciary Buildings Service and the Judicial Space and Facilities Management Fund, outlines strict congressional approval thresholds for projects, mandates regular reporting and audits, and sets a sunset timeline for the authorities granted.

affected_groups.effect: Gains new authority to establish a Judiciary Buildings Service, manage real property and leases in pilot districts and the Thurgood Marshall Federal Judiciary Building, and oversee financial funds and audits.
affected_groups.group: Administrative Office of the United States Courts and the Director

affected_groups.effect: Must transfer requested properties and leases to the Director, provide necessary transition and building management information, and receive rent or reimbursements for maintained court accommodations.
Accommodated by the Judiciary's own building management structure in pilot districts, with priority for contiguous space and utilization of the Thurgood Marshall Federal Judiciary Building.

key_provisions: Establishes a pilot program for the Director to identify real property containing court accommodations in up to 10 judicial districts for transfer of jurisdiction, custody, and control.
Creates the Judiciary Buildings Service to acquire, manage, operate, alter, construct, and lease space and facilities necessary for court accommodations.
Transfers jurisdiction, custody, and control of the Thurgood Marshall Federal Judiciary Building to the Director 181 days after enactment.

Establishes the Judicial Space and Facilities Management Fund in the Treasury to finance acquisitions, alterations, construction, management, and rent or reimbursements to the General Services Administration.
Requires congressional committee resolutions and prospectuses for construction, purchase, acquisition, or alteration projects exceeding specific monetary thresholds indexed to inflation.
Directs the Comptroller General to conduct a biennial review and report to Congress on the operations, procurement, contracting processes, and fund usage of the Judiciary Buildings Service.
Sets a sunset timeline where transfer authority ceases after 7 years, asset transfers back to GSA begin after 10 years, and the Act is fully repealed after 15 years.
missing_information: The specific names of the 10 judicial districts selected for the pilot program.
The exact financial baseline or specific monetary amounts currently allocated for rent under existing GSA management before the transition.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Judicial Space and Facilities Management Effectiveness Act of 2026 establishes a pilot program allowing the Director of the Administrative Office of the United States Courts to take over jurisdiction, custody, and control of real property and leases containing court accommodations in up to ten judicial districts. It also transfers the Thurgood Marshall Federal Judiciary Building to the Director's control, creates the Judiciary Buildings Service and the Judicial Space and Facilities Management Fund, outlines strict congressional approval thresholds for projects, mandates regular reporting and audits, and sets a sunset timeline for the authorities granted.
summary_detail.significance: This bill modifies how real property and facilities for the federal judiciary are managed by shifting certain custodial and operational controls from the General Services Administration to the judicial branch on a pilot basis, supported by dedicated funding, independent audits, and congressional oversight.
